subject: POC scope reset and updated acceptance criteria — DataSentry trial
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Lara Cohen <lara.cohen@datasentry.com>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@datasentry.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: POC kickoff recap & proposed success criteria (next steps attached)

Hi Lara / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned going into the trial week:

1) Scope (as discussed):
   - Live API inference for intent classification on the Transit use case (3k daily requests).
   - Embeddings for semantic search on the Operations KB (index ~150k docs).

2) Proposed acceptance criteria (initial):
   - Intent classification F1 >= 0.88 on held-out set (500 examples).
   - 95th percentile latency < 200ms for single-request interactive flows.
   - Embedding similarity MAP >= 0.82 for the evaluation set (100 queries).

3) Timeline / ownership:
   - 03/05: Redwood deploys trial model variant + sample index (Monica).
   - 03/06–03/12: DataSentry runs evaluation tests (Lara/Tom).
   - 03/13: Review results and decide go/no-go (all).

I’ve attached the POC_plan_v1.pdf and a simple eval matrix. Please review and confirm ownership or call out changes. If you want to add an extra use case we can discuss trade-offs to keep the timeline.

Thanks —
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: POC_plan_v1.pdf
From: Lara Cohen <lara.cohen@datasentry.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@datasentry.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 08:34:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff recap & proposed success criteria (next steps attached)

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick note from our side after internal sync: we want to add a second intent (escalation routing) into the classification scope — it’s a high-impact item for our product and would make the POC more representative.

Concerns:
- Adding the new intent will increase the labeled set requirements. We can provide ~250 labeled examples for the escalation intent by 03/07, but that tightens the test schedule.
- We’re also interested in a soft uptime check (simulated burst to 50 RPS) to validate autoscale behavior — if Redwood can include that, it would be very helpful for our infra team.

Can you confirm whether we can absorb the escalation intent without shifting the review date? If not, propose a minimal plan to re-baseline.

Best,
Lara
Senior PM, Platform | DataSentry
lara.cohen@datasentry.com
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Lara Cohen <lara.cohen@datasentry.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff recap & proposed success criteria (next steps attached)

Hi Lara —

Thanks — short answer: yes, we can include the escalation routing intent, but it will affect the evaluation matrix and likely the pass/fail thresholds for the classification metric because of class balance. Proposed re-baselined plan below (minimal disruption):

- Scope update: include Escalation intent (we’ll retrain the label-weighted head).
- Data deadline: 03/07 EOD for labeled escalation examples (you indicated ~250).
- Eval adjustments: expand held-out test set to 700 examples (includes new intent). Target F1 adjusted to >= 0.86 given class imbalance.
- Autoscale smoke test: Redwood will run a simulated burst test to 50 RPS on 03/10 at 10:00 PT (Neha to coordinate).
- Review date: keep 03/13 for result review; if data arrives late, push to 03/16 at the latest.

I’ve updated the eval matrix and attached updated_eval_matrix_v2.xlsx. If that works, Rishi can update the HubSpot deal notes and I’ll schedule the autoscale window.

Thanks —
Monica
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Lara Cohen <lara.cohen@datasentry.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff recap & proposed success criteria (next steps attached)

Hi team —

Quick logistics for the autoscale smoke test on 03/10:
- I’ll provision the test harness and a short-lived dedicated capacity token for the window (no production keys).
- We’ll run three bursts: 10s @ 20 RPS, 30s @ 50 RPS, and 60s @ 30 RPS to observe warmup and KV cache behavior.
- I’ll collect 50/90/95/99 percentile latencies and token costs and share the runbook before the test.

Action items for DataSentry: please confirm the test time (default 10:00 PT) and provide the sample payload format for the escalation examples.

-Neha
Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
From: Lara Cohen <lara.cohen@datasentry.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@datasentry.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 11:27:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff recap & proposed success criteria (next steps attached)

Hi all —

That plan looks good — we can deliver the 250 escalation labels by EOD 03/07 and 10:00 PT on 03/10 works for the burst tests (Tom will share payload format by 03/06).

We appreciate the flexibility on the acceptance threshold. Confirming:
- New target F1 >= 0.86 on combined intent set (700 examples).
- Autoscale burst window 03/10 10:00 PT.
- Review 03/13 — if any delays, we’ll notify immediately.

Looking forward to the test run.

Best,
Lara
Senior PM, Platform | DataSentry

Forwarded attachments: updated_eval_matrix_v2.xlsx
